Q: Can an objectURL point to an on-disk cache file rather than loading the file into memory? A:

No — createObjectURL only takes a Blob/File, and there's no handle to a Cache entry's backing file. Note Blobs aren't necessarily in RAM anyway; Chrome and Firefox spill large blobs to disk. If the goal is avoiding the copy entirely, use a Service Worker to intercept the normal URL and respond from caches.match() — then you keep the original src and never materialize a Blob.

Q: Campaign Monitor links don't work in Outlook 365 A:

Sync the CTA links via Campaign Monitor's API before each send — after updating the URL in the WYSIWYG, pull the campaign HTML, copy the updated <a href> value into the <v:roundrect href>, then push the corrected HTML back before sending.

This keeps the VML button intact (so Outlook desktop keeps its proper styling) while ensuring both links stay in sync, without relying on the shakier approach of stripping the VML href and depending on an <a> nested inside it.

One caveat: worth confirming Campaign Monitor's API actually supports this campaign content/template update operation before building around it — the sync logic itself is sound, it's just the API capability that needs verifying first.

Q: PyCharm type hinting constraining improperly? A:

It's a PyCharm bug, not you missing anything, mypy and pyright both pass this clean. PyCharm's narrowing seems to key off the bare name "val" instead of the actual symbol, so once it decides val is None inside that if block, it slaps the same None onto anything else spelled val, ValObj.val included. Cast it and move on:

from typing import cast
new_val = cast(int, ValObj.val)

Q: How to Zoom with Axes3D in Matplotlib A:

I have found that in matplotlib 3.3.4 you can in fact use the left (not right to perform zoom in) button in the mouse to draw a rectangle and after the zooming process unplug the right button. After this, the image will be zoomed out.

At least it's the case if for matplotlib use:

  • matplotlib.use("Qt5Agg")
  • and for navigation toolbar use matplotlib.backends.backend_qt5agg.NavigationToolbar2QT.
